title: Mechanical Energy
seo_title: Grade 10 Physical Sciences: Mechanical Energy Worksheets (CAPS)
standard_text: Gravitational potential energy, Eₚ = mgh; kinetic energy, Eₖ = ½mv²; mechanical energy, Eₘ = Eₚ + Eₖ; the principle of conservation of mechanical energy in the absence of friction. (summary of CAPS Physical Sciences, Grade 10, Physics: Energy)
meta_desc: Free Grade 10 Physical Sciences worksheets (CAPS): gravitational potential energy, kinetic energy, mechanical energy and the conservation of mechanical energy. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Without friction, mechanical energy is conserved.
body_html:
How to think about it

Gravitational potential energy is the energy an object has because of its position: Eₚ = mgh, with g = 9,8 m·s⁻². Kinetic energy is the energy of motion: Eₖ = ½mv².

Mechanical energy is the sum Eₚ + Eₖ. If there is no friction or air resistance, mechanical energy is conserved: as a ball falls, potential energy changes into kinetic energy, so (Eₚ + Eₖ) at the top = (Eₚ + Eₖ) at the bottom.

Example

A 2 kg book is 1,5 m above the floor. Eₚ?

mgh

Answer: 2 × 9,8 × 1,5 = 29,4 J

Example

A 1 000 kg car moves at 10 m·s⁻¹. Eₖ?

½mv²

Answer: 50 000 J

Common mistakes

  • Forgetting to square v.
  • Using the mass in grams.
  • Thinking mechanical energy is conserved when there is friction.

faq.q: Does a heavy object fall faster than a light one?
faq.a: No; without air resistance both fall with the same acceleration, because Eₚ and Eₖ both depend on m.

faq.q: Where does the energy go when friction acts?
faq.a: It becomes thermal energy (and sound), so mechanical energy decreases.
